sentences.text: On The 6th Of April, 2026
Misc . Appeal No. 1330 of 2025

Mangilal
 Versus
 Mukesh And Others
 Appearance:
 Shri Shyamlal Patidar - Advocate for the appellant.
 Shri Rajesh Pandit with Shri Sudarshan Pandit - Advocate
respondent No.3 / Insurance Company.

Order 
This Misc. Appeal under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 has been filed by the appellant assailing the impugned award dated 22/11/2024 passed by III Member, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Dhar (M.P.) in MACC No. 461/2023, whereby an amount of Rs.7,14,030/- along with interest @ 6% has been awarded to the appellant / claimant - injured, who has suffered grievous injuries in a road traffic accident occurred on 29/01/2023 involving the offending vehicle bearing registration number MP-12-GB-3099.
2.
Learned counsel for the appellant / injured submits that in the accident appellant has sustained grievous injuries.
Appellant has suffered fracture of Spine D-12 Vertebra in the accident.
He was NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-IND:9032 2 MA-1330-2025 operated and implants were inserted.
Due to the injuries, appellant suffered Paraplegia.
For this, Doctor Dr. Devendra Mandloi (AW-3) has been examined, who has issued Disability Certificate (Ex.-P/24) certifying that appellant has suffered 100% permanent disability.

He further submits that looking to the injuries and the hardship suffered by the appellant, the amount awarded by the learned Claims Tribunal in the heads of Pain and Suffering, Special Diet, Attendant and Transportation is on lower side.
2.1

Learned counsel further submits that since the appellant has suffered 100% permanent disability, therefore, 40% future prospects is to be added by taking Rs.5,000/- per month as expenses towards attendant and applying multiplier of 5 as has been ascertained to calculate the permanent disability.
To buttress his contention learned counsel has placed reliance on the judgment by the Apex Court in the case of Abhimanyu Pratap Singh Vs. Namita Sekhon and Another reported in 2022 ACJ 1995 .

entities.text: Abhimanyu Pratap Singh Vs. Namita Sekhon and Another reported in 2022 ACJ 1995
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: On these submissions, learned counsel prays for allowing the appeal by enhancing the award amount as prayed for.

Mangilal vs Mukesh on 6 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/22830349/
1 3 .
Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent / Insurance Company has opposed the prayer on the ground that evidence led before the learned Claims Tribunal has been rightly appreciated.
The amount awarded by the learned Claims Tribunal is just and proper and no enhancement is required.

All the factors have been considered by the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-IND:9032 3 MA-1330-2025 learned Claims Tribunal while awarding the compensation amount and no fault can be found with in the impugned award.
Hence, prays for dismissal of the appeal being devoid of any substance.

4. Heard and considered the rival submissions raised at bar by learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
5.

From perusal of the record, it is apparent that appellant has suffered 100% permanent disability and disability has been proved by Dr. Devendra Mandloi (AW-3), who has given Disability Certificate (Ex.-P/24).

Looking to the disability suffered by the appellant, this Court is of the view that the amount awarded by the learned Claims Tribunal in the heads of Pain and Suffering, Special Diet and Transportation is on lower side and the same requires enhancement, therefore, the compensation amount in these heads is enhanced to Rs.1,00,000/-, Rs.15,000/- and Rs.15,000/-
respectively.

6. Keeping in view the judgment in the case of Abhimanyu Pratap Singh (Supra) and on the basis of the evidence available on record it is established that appellant has suffered 100% permanent disability and for the life time he will need assistance of attender to meet out his daily chores,
therefore, considering the monthly expenses of Rs.5,000/- and applying multiplier of 5 for 12 months, Rs.3,00,000/- awarded towards attendant expenses.
The amount awarded in the other heads needs no interference.

7. Accordingly, the just and proper compensation amount comes NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-IND:9032 4 MA-1330-2025 as under:
Rs.9,325/- pm x 12 months x 5 Permanent Disability: (Multiplier) = Rs.5,59,500/-
(100% PD) Pain and Suffering: Rs.1,00,000/-
 Special Diet: Rs.15,000/-
 Transportation: Rs.15,000/-

Medical Expenses: Rs.44,530/-
 Future Treatment  Rs.10,000/-
 Expenses:
 Attendant Expenses: Rs.3,00,000/-
 Total: Rs.10,44,030/-

MACT Awarded: Rs.7,14,030/-
 Enhanced Amount: Rs.3,30,000/-
Thus, the just and proper amount of compensation in the instant case is Rs.10,44,030/- as against the award of the Tribunal of Rs.7,14,030/-.

Accordingly,
the appellant is entitled to an enhanced amount of Rs.3,30,000/- over and above the Mangilal vs Mukesh on 6 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/22830349/
2 amount which has been awarded by the Tribunal.
8.
Resultantly, the appeal filed by the appellant / claimant is allowed to the extent as indicated hereinabove.
Other terms and conditions of the impugned award including rate of interest @ 6% shall remain intact.
The enhanced amount shall also carry interest at the same rate.
(BINOD KUMAR DWIVEDI) JUDGE Tej Mangilal vs Mukesh on 6 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/22830349/
